newsitem.title: FRANCE: Six held over Corsica bomb, extortion.
newsitem.headline: Six held over Corsica bomb, extortion.

text.p: Six people were in detention on Saturday, suspected of involvement in an extortion racket by Corsican separatists and a bomb attack on a golf club on the French Mediterranean island, the Interior Ministry said.

Suspected separatists made two new bomb attacks in northern Corsica overnight, including one against a garage used by paramilitary gendarmes. No one was hurt in the incidents on an island battered by 20 years of guerrilla violence.
In a rare crackdown on guerrillas -- despite repeated government pledges of toughness -- the Interior Ministry said six people had been arrested in Paris and on Corsica itself.

A statement said the detentions followed a bid by the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) to extort cash from the Sperone golf club in southern Corsica and a subsequent bomb attack by five people on the course keeper's home on Thursday.
The bomb flattened the building but hurt no one. The FLNC claimed responsibilty for the bombing, accusing the golf course owners of letting French commandos use the building.
Justice sources said on Friday that 12 people were initially rounded up.
La Chaine Info television said the bomb was planted after the golf course owners refused to pay 4.0 million ($780,000) to the guerrillas and denounced the extortion to the authorities.
In attacks overnight on Corsica, a bomb damaged the door of a garage attached to a gendarmerie barracks in the northern town of Murato late on Friday, police said.
Early on Saturday, explosive charges blew out the metallic grille and the door of a depot selling car parts in Furiani.
